author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
China and America are talking again. There are leaders’ meetings, phone calls and a new channel for discussing artificial intelligence. Officials are cautiously trying to keep the relationship from veering into crisis.
And yet some of the hardest questions remain untouched.
Neither side is giving much ground on advanced chips, export controls remain a battlefield and neither Washington nor Beijing appears ready to slow its race to develop increasingly powerful AI.
So what, exactly, does it mean...
title: A US scholar’s take on how shifts in US-China relations are felt in a Tsinghua classroom

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Japan is increasingly turning to foreign companies to accelerate its military modernisation, drawing on overseas technology, expertise and production capacity to plug defence gaps that could prove critical in a potential regional conflict involving China.
The push has gathered momentum over the past week, with Tokyo confirming a contract for Ukrainian interceptor drones and a multinational fighter consortium preparing to expand its design operations in Japan.
French defence giant Thales is also...
title: Japan taps foreign tech to plug defence gaps as China’s power grows. Will it pay off?

author: Dannie Peng
description:
China’s R&D investment grew by 8.2 per cent last year – fuelled by double-digit growth in fundamental science and university funding – in sharp contrast with deep budget cuts across the US research sector.
Total investment in research and experimental development crossed 3.9 trillion yuan (US$583 billion) in 2025, “maintaining a trajectory of steady growth”, the National Bureau of Statistics said when releasing the data on Friday.
State news agency Xinhua noted on Friday that in the five years...
title: China’s R&D spending keeps up steady rise as No 1 US seeks further funding cuts

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese scientists have unearthed a fossil of the earliest known flightless bird, offering compelling evidence that not all early birds evolved to take to the skies.
The discovery could also challenge long-held assumptions – including ideas dating back to evolutionary theorist Charles Darwin – that flightlessness in birds arose only as a secondary adaptation after earlier species had mastered flight.
The 150 million-year-old fossil of the Late Jurassic avialan Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis found in...
title: Sorry, Darwin: Chinese fossil shows that not all early birds evolved to fly

author: Carol Yang
description:
In talks with Israel’s president on Thursday, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called for an immediate easing of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza and for Israel to reverse its West Bank settlement expansion.
“The imperative priority is to fully open access routes into Gaza. Two million civilians must not be left to struggle on the brink of survival, nor can this humanitarian catastrophe be allowed to spread,” Wang said, according to a Chinese foreign ministry statement on Friday.
The meeting with...
title: China urges Israel to end West Bank settlement expansion and ease Gaza crisis

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
Beijing has invited White House press secretary Katie Zacharia to visit the country more often after she said in an interview that China “doesn’t even have proper toilets”.
The newly appointed spokeswoman for the Trump administration made the controversial remarks in an interview on Thursday with conservative commentator Jack Posobiec, when talking about the perception around 2016 that “the gold days, the glory days of the US were over and China was on the horizon”.
“I remember this very...
title: China invites Trump press secretary Katie Zacharia to visit after ‘proper toilets’ slur

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China revealed AI-powered drone interceptors and other uncrewed systems at an international counterterrorism forum in Beijing this week, as security experts warned that new technologies could enable new forms of terrorism.
The equipment was on display at the Great Wall-2026 International Forum on Counterterrorism, which ran from Tuesday to Thursday and was attended by more than 320 defence experts and military delegates from 62 countries.
Discussions focused on how advances in artificial...
title: China leans in to hi-tech systems to counter emerging AI-fuelled terror threats

author: Raymond Ma,Neil Denslow
description:
European Union leaders supported creating a tool to potentially shut out Chinese goods as a growing flood of low-cost imports pushed the bilateral trade deficit to a record.
Officials could start work on developing a trade “kill switch”, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen signalled to EU leaders at a Brussels meeting on Thursday, the South China Morning Post reported, citing unidentified people briefed on the talks. Leaders requested a proposal by year-end, Bloomberg News said....
title: EU backs trade ‘kill switch’, China exports surge, third-quarter GDP

author: Shi Huang
description:
Li Renke, a visionary cardiovascular scientist who applied engineering principles to the human heart and developed conductive biomaterials to repair tissue damaged by heart attacks, died while attending an academic conference in the Chinese city of Xian earlier this month. He was 65.
His death on October 10 was announced by The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (CUHK-Shenzhen), where he was presidential chair professor and associate dean of research and translation at the school of...
title: Pioneering heart stem cell expert Li Renke dies at 65 during a Chinese conference

author: Fan Chen
description:
The Chinese ambassador to the Philippines says Beijing could “easily win” should it use force in the region but instead chooses peace, remarks that have drawn sharp criticism from Manila and calls for diplomatic restraint.
The war of words came as tension over the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea rises, with Beijing repeatedly driving away Philippine aircraft over the shoal in recent months, most recently about two weeks ago, while accusing Manila of violating Chinese...
title: Envoy says China could ‘easily win’ conflict as Manila claims it is ‘thinly veiled threat’

author: SCMP
description:
We have selected seven stories from this week’s news across Hong Kong, mainland China, the wider Asia region and beyond that resonated with our readers and shed light on topical issues. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. Chinese scientists say they spotted possible Israeli electronic warfare units
Chinese military scientists claim they have developed an algorithm that could help identify electronic warfare units using civil aviation flight data.
2....
title: China maps Israeli spoofing with flight data; new US press secretary: SCMP’s 7 highlights

author: Alcott Wei
description:
President Xi Jinping has pledged to “uproot sick trees” in the anti-corruption fight, according to a speech transcript published by the party’s flagship magazine ahead of a major party conclave later this month.
The warning appeared on Thursday in the magazine Qiushi, which carried fresh details of a speech Xi delivered in January at the fifth plenary session of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI), the party’s top anti-corruption watchdog.
The speech contained a series of...
title: Xi’s pledge to ‘uproot sick trees’ aired weeks ahead of major party conclave

author: Bernard Chan
description:
The most consequential outcome of President Xi Jinping’s Washington visit might be his US counterpart Donald Trump’s unusually lavish welcome. It told Beijing, US allies and global markets that, however fierce the strategic rivalry, China’s importance makes sustained diplomatic engagement essential.
The airport greeting, lavish banquet at the White House and flyover by military aircraft restored the appearance of a workable relationship between two powers. Even so, Beijing has learned not to...
title: Pageantry matters for US-China summits, even with modest results

author: Caroline Lin
description:
A 500-year-old Buddha statue that was found buried by a roadside in Australia has been returned to China, leaving an ongoing mystery about how it arrived in the country.
The 15cm (six-inch) bronze figurine was formally handed over to Chinese consular representatives during a ceremony in the coastal town of Denham in Shark Bay on Tuesday, the public broadcaster ABC reported.
It will be taken to China for further evaluation to establish its history before being displayed at a museum in...
title: Australia hands Ming dynasty Buddha back to China amid ongoing mystery over its arrival

author: Dewey Sim,Khushboo Razdan
description:
Japan’s hopes for a visit by Donald Trump during his trip to Asia next month may be hanging in the balance as relations between China and the United States steadily improve.
The US president spent three days in Japan ahead of last year’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, and his meeting with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi was hailed as a sign of a “new golden age” in the countries’ relationship.
But since then Trump’s growing rapport with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping has caused...
title: Why Japanese PM Takaichi is still keen to roll out the welcome mat for Trump
